articles.title: Horoscope for Tuesday, July 21, 2026
articles.description:
Moon alert

Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 5:30 to 9 a.m. Chicago time. After that, the moon moves from Libra into Scorpio.

Aries (March 21-April 19)

A positive day

Financial speculation might be rewarding today. Meanwhile, expect surprise invitations to socialize. You might also suddenly decide about a vacation or a future sports event. Relations with kids will be spontaneous and fun.

Taurus (April 20-May 20)

An average day

Avoid power struggles with partners, spouses and close friends today. Nevertheless, something special or favorable or financially attractive might benefit your family today. You might buy something for your home or receive a gift — or your family might have a new addition.

Gemini (May 21-June 20)

A positive day

Spontaneous short trips and opportunities to meet new faces and see new places will please you today. Meanwhile, work-related discussions might be challenging. Steer clear of controversial subjects like politics and religion because they could turn nasty. Stay calm.

Cancer (June 21-July 22)

A positive day

This is a financially fortuitous day for you. You might suddenly make more money or get a bit richer for some reason. If you have a chance to pursue a new job offer or ask for a raise, do it. Meanwhile, be patient with your kids and romantic partners to avoid arguments.

Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)

A positive day

An encounter with a friend or a member of a group might surprise you today because it turns out to be something other than what you expected. It might broaden your horizons in some way or increase your connections. Perhaps you will meet a new friend. Meanwhile, be patient at home.

Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)

An average day

Avoid arguments with daily contacts, siblings and relatives, especially if you are trying hard to make a point or convince others to agree with you. Give it up. Instead, focus on some inner realizations that might occur today — perhaps an epiphany? Listen to your inner world.

Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)

A positive day

A friendship might delight you today. Or perhaps you'll become involved with an organization or club in a new way. Whatever happens will be unexpected and sudden. Meanwhile, avoid disagreements about money and possessions. Be smart.

Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)

An average day

Today you might give in to impulsive or compulsive behavior. You might also encounter an emotional power struggle with someone — perhaps because someone is reacting to something that makes you suddenly look good? Something unexpected favors you! This might be jealousy.

Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)

A positive day

Unexpected opportunities to travel might fall into your lap today. If so, act quickly — this window of opportunity will be brief. Likewise, a chance to explore something in publishing, medicine, the law or higher education might also appear out of nowhere. Act fast.

Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19)

An average day

Avoid money squabbles today or arguments about possessions. Instead, keep your eyes open because you might benefit in practical ways or financial ways through the wealth and resources of someone else. Or you might get money back from the government. Could be anything. Ka-ching!

Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18)

An average day

You're high-viz today, which is why it's in your best interest not to have a public argument somewhere. Why end up with egg on your face? Instead, focus on partnerships and close relationships because something unexpected will delight you. Be open to whatever happens.

Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20)

An average day

Steer clear of controversial subjects today because they could become emotionally charged. Meanwhile, this is a great day to suddenly improve your health or your job. Your chance to do so will have a very short window, so if something arises be prepared to act fast. Something that is pet-related might also delight you.

If today is your birthday

Actor and comedian Robin Williams (1951-2014) shares your birthday. You are both extroverted and introverted. You're curious, determined and independent-thinking. You have an extraordinary understanding of human nature. This is a slower-paced year. It's OK to rest and rejuvenate your energy. Focus on relationships with those who are kind, helpful and supportive.

articles.title: Country diary: I’m immersed in the rich, chromatic aura of a summer meadow | Mark Cocker
articles.description: Hartington Meadows, Derbyshire: Amid a complex reticulation of stalks, stems, blooms and leaves, the right response might be to drop down before it In his glorious poem Haymaking , about a flower meadow, Edward Thomas describes how the fiery day “had a kernel sweet of cold” and “the white empty road was lightly strewn/With leaves”. The heat here, however, was unrelieved, and if the road was empty, it was also liquefying at its margin. Sweat banded my cap and ran in the creases at the backs of my bare legs, where, I noticed, the horseflies focused their attentions. Flower meadows, more than any other British land form, seem to be the most entangled and entangling places we have. They encircle and almost invade you with a sense of richness: not just the entwining hum of insect wings, nor the penetrating chromatic songs of the flowers themselves, but in an exuberant aura of living abundance. articles.title: Four beluga whales on way to Shedd from closed Canadian park: report
articles.description:
Four beluga whales from a shuttered aquatic park in Niagara Falls, Canada, were on their way to Shedd Aquarium Monday as part of an “unprecedented rescue effort,” according to Canadian media.

Two more whales were headed to SeaWorld in San Antonio Monday, according to The Canadian Press.

It’s the first phase of a plan to move up to 30 belugas over the next few weeks from Marineland to several American aquariums as well as to Oceanografic Valencia in Spain. Earlier this month, Shedd announced it could receive as many as 10 belugas from Marineland.

Shedd officials declined Monday to offer a timeline for when the whales would arrive at the aquarium or to confirm Canadian press reports that they were in fact on their way to Chicago.

“As reported, an initial rescue of the belugas at Marineland of Canada is under way. This is a complex rescue operation and experts are focused on the immediate safety and comfort of the animals involved. The group of accredited aquariums will share more details and updates as animals arrive safely to their new homes,” said Kayley Galassini, Shedd’s director of public relations.

The belugas headed to Shedd are named Sierra, Acadia, Osiris and Lillooet, The Canadian Press reported.

The future of the beluga whales has been in doubt since Marineland closed to the public in 2024. Marineland has previously threatened to euthanize the sea mammals, citing a lack of funding to care for them.

In June, the Canadian government signed off on the plan to send the belugas to the American and Spanish aquariums. Earlier this month, U.S. authorities followed suit and signed off on the plan.

Twenty whales — 19 belugas and one killer whale — have died at Marineland since 2019, according to provincial government data obtained through freedom-of-information laws and official statements, the Associated Press reported.

The planned move to the aquariums is controversial, with some animal rights advocates arguing that the belugas are being exported potentially in violation of a 2019 Canadian law that bans the breeding of marine mammals in captivity.

--

articles.title: Skepticism grows after MAGA-linked farm cleared in parasite outbreak
articles.description: Taylor Farms claimed Monday the FDA apologized for incorrectly linking the California-based farm to a cyclospora parasitic outbreak that sickened over 1,645 people and hospitalized 141. The parasite is known for causing watery or explosive diarrhea, according to Cleveland Clinic . The company had voluntarily recalled Mexican-grown iceberg lettuce Sunday based on FDA guidance, but stated Monday, "Today, we were informed that the FDA made a mistake and this was a false positive." "To be clear, at this moment, FDA has not identified a single positive product test result for Cyclospora," they continued. "Our thoughts remain with everyone who has fallen ill in this outbreak," the company added, "We are committed to working with public health authorities as the ongoing outbreak investigation continues." The Centers for Disease Control is investigating more than 5,100 additional illnesses. The FDA's reversal drew skepticism after Taylor Farms executives reportedly met with White House officials Thursday to distance themselves from the outbreak. Critics questioned the FDA's credibility, with writer Nathan Newman speculating , "Like most people, I assume FDA is lying here to help a big Trump donor And this is horrifying." Health policy analyst Jenn Kaufman warned , "This unfortunately will only further erode confidence in the CDC and public health." Watch the video below. Your browser does not support the video tag.
